title: Reel: Indy metro has 21.3% more homes for sale, what that means for winter buyers
hook: If your home search stalled last winter because nothing fit, this winter looks different.
body: If your home search stalled last winter because nothing fit, this winter looks different. In October, 7,171 homes were for sale across the Indy metro. That's 21.3% more than a year earlier. For you, more listings means more room to compare and less need to rush. You can see a home twice, ask questions about the price, and walk away from one that doesn't fit. It also means a plan matters, because more homes take more sorting. We can narrow the field in Fishers, Carmel or Noblesville to the homes that match your budget and your commute. Call 317-863-9011 and ask for a winter home short list.

title: Reel: Buying in Fishers from out of state, what to ask a relocation agent
hook: How do you buy a home in Fishers when you still live in another state?
body: How do you buy a home in Fishers when you still live in another state? Start with the agent you hire, and ask a few direct questions. How will you help me compare Fishers with Carmel, Noblesville and Westfield, from commutes to property taxes? How will I see homes before I can fly in? Listen for live video tours and quick replies. And who keeps inspections, the appraisal and closing on track while I'm still packing? Clear answers tell you a lot. Vague answers tell you more. Call 317-863-9011 and book a 15-minute video call comparing Fishers, Carmel and Westfield.

title: Reel: Hamilton County median list price $445,000, down 6.3%, the pricing takeaway
hook: What should you list your Fishers or Carmel home for this winter?
body: What should you list your Fishers or Carmel home for this winter? Start here. Hamilton County's median list price was $445,000 in October, down 6.3% from a year earlier. Buyers also have more homes to compare than they did last fall, so they notice fast when a price was set from last spring's headlines. A price built from today's comparable homes, on your street and in your home's condition, gives buyers a reason to book the showing. One note: these are asking prices, not what homes closed for. Call 317-863-9011 and ask for a winter pricing check on your home.

title: Reel: Are prices going up or down in your town? Reading the headlines (text-list format)
hook: One Noblesville headline says prices are down, another says they're up, and both can be right.
body: One Noblesville headline says prices are down, another says they're up, and both can be right. Ask three things first. Is it a list price or a closed price? What's the time frame, and is it compared with the same month last year? And what's being measured? A real example: across the Indy metro in October, the median list price was lower than a year earlier, but list price per square foot was up 5.1%. Same market, two headlines. A shift toward smaller homes can pull the median down while each square foot is priced higher. Comment your town below, and we'll reply with the number to watch there.
cta: Comment your town below, and we'll reply with the number to watch there.

title: Reel: The model home sales rep works for the builder (new construction walk-and-talk)
hook: The friendly sales rep at the model home works for the builder, not for you.
body: The friendly sales rep at the model home works for the builder, not for you. It's simply their job to sell the builder's homes on the builder's terms. If you want someone reviewing the contract, the upgrades and the timeline with your interests in mind, bring your own agent. Here's the catch. Some builders ask that your agent be registered at your very first visit. So if you're starting model home visits this winter, ask about that policy before you walk in. On our team, Derek Evelo is the new construction specialist. Call 317-863-9011 and ask Derek to register as your agent before your first model home visit.

title: Reel: Latest data shows fewer Indy-area homes going under contract, the seller takeaway
hook: In the latest month of data, fewer Indy-area homes went under contract, even with more for sale.
body: In the latest month of data, fewer Indy-area homes went under contract, even with more for sale. In October, pending listings across the metro were down 12% from a year earlier. If you're planning to sell in Fishers, Carmel or Westfield early next year, here's what that means. Buyers are taking their time and comparing homes side by side. So your home needs to make its case from the first day: a price set from today's comparable homes, clear photos, and small repairs finished before the listing goes live, not after the first round of feedback. Call 317-863-9011 and ask for a pre-listing checklist for your home.
